name: Beechjet 400 / Hawker 400XP / T-1 Jayhawk
summary: Light jet derived from the Mitsubishi Diamond; the USAF's T-1A Jayhawk trainer version was retired in 2026, so the US fleet is now civil.

engines: Two Pratt & Whitney Canada JT15D turbofans in pods high on the rear fuselage
fuselage: Short, fairly deep fuselage with small windows
tail: T-tail with a swept fin and swept horizontal stabilizer

tellTales: Swept wing with plain tips on a small T-tail twinjet
Short, deep fuselage with small windows
Engines mounted high on the rear fuselage close below the tail

confusedWith.howToTell: The Beechjet/Hawker 400 has plain wingtips and no ventral fins; the Learjet 45 has winglets and small ventral fins under the tail.
The Beechjet/Hawker 400 has plain wingtips; the Learjet 35 has tip tanks (or winglets on the 31).
The Beechjet/Hawker 400 has a T-tail; the Hawker 800 has its tailplane partway up the fin and oval windows.
The Beechjet/Hawker 400 has plain wingtips and small windows; the Phenom 300 has winglets and very large windows.

usCount.source: Production (~600 Diamond/Beechjet/400XP civil) with ~70% US-registered per FAA registry / JETNET (approx.); USAF T-1A retired Aug 2026
